intro: Lesson 30. Read the case, then plan your analysis.

passage.title: The Rahma Hotel
paras: The Rahma Hotel has 40 rooms, a halal restaurant and 25 staff, most paid the National Minimum Wage. It is 400 metres from a city station.

The government has announced a new high-speed rail line that will stop at the station in four years' time. Journeys to the capital will fall from 2 hours 10 minutes to 55 minutes. Building work around the station will last three years, with road closures.
Two national hotel chains have already asked to build near the station.
passage.source: All businesses, people and figures in this case are fictional, made up for practice.

blocks.h: Answer frame (6 marks: chains of reasoning in context)

blocks.text: Analyse how the new high-speed rail line could affect the Rahma Hotel. (6 marks)

frame.label: Chain: because ... this leads to ... so ...
Chain: because ... this leads to ... so ...

markScheme.a: More visitors and business travellers once journeys fall to 55 minutes, so occupancy and restaurant sales rise; but three years of building and road closures may put guests off, and new chain hotels increase competition, so prices and profit may fall. Level 3 (5-6): a balanced analysis with two developed chains of reasoning, both in context. Level 2 (3-4): developed reasoning, partly in context. Level 1 (1-2): points identified with little development.
